thread.title: Markets Seek Direction as Twitter Soars, Teva Tumbles

author: Ben Levisohn
title: Markets Seek Direction as Twitter Soars, Teva Tumbles
text:
Stocks look set for a slightly higher open this morning even as the 10-year Treasury yield continued to tick higher following a stronger-than-expected jobless-claims report . Congress is still working to complete a budget deal that will get a vote in the Senate today.
Illustration: Getty Images S&P 500 futures imply an advance of 0.1%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures suggest a relatively unchanged open. Nasdaq Composite futures imply a gained 0.3% at the open. The 10-year Treasury year has ticked up 0.043 percentage point to 2.875%.
The number of Americans filing for unemployment insurance fell to 221,000 last week , below economist forecasts for 230,000. The drop brings the four-week average to 225,000, the lowest since 1973, writes Bleakley Advisory Group's Peter Boockvar. "The consistent fall in the supply of labor has employers holding on tight to their existing ones and that is writ large in the smallest level of claims in 45 years," he explains. "The wage response is still spotty but still seems to be bubbling up with green shoots."
The news caused the 10-year Treasury yield to rise, but not by much, and the action seems to suggest that the market could handle a gradual rise, if not a quick one. Still, the markets really did break early this week, and Rhino Trading's Michael Block suggests it could take a little while before markets return to normal (whatever that is). "The thing about cleaning up a mess like we saw earlier in the week is that you think you have every speck of dirt and broken glass mopped up, but inevitably you miss a spot or someone comes rushing in and slips and falls and gets blood all over your nice clean floor so you have to circle back and mop that up too," Block writes. "That’s really the best analogy I can think of right now for what’s going on here."
It'll do for now.
Morning Movers Alexion Pharmaceuticals (ALXN) has fallen 2.7% to $114 after reporting a profit of $1.48 a share, beating forecasts for $1.09 , on sales of $909.7 million, ahead of analyst predictions for $878 million. Alexion also said it would earn between $6.60 a share and $6.80 a share in 2018, below estimates for $7.07 a share. "While all key products (Soliris, Strensiq, and even Kanuma), delivered solid performance in 4Q, management established 2018 guidance that was below consensus on both the top- and bottom-line, which, in our view, might not be well-received by the Street," writes SunTrust analyst Yatin Suneja.
Coty (COTY) has soared 12% to $19.62 after reporting a profit of 32 cents on sales of $2.64 billion. Analysts had been predicting earnings of 23 cents a share on revenue of $2.48 billion. "Shares were very weak into the print and given the solid top-line beat, we would expect a strong relief rally today," writes Wells Fargo analyst Joe Lachky.
Edgewell Personal Care (EPC) has dropped 4.4% to $50.13 after reporting an adjusted 20 cents a share, well below forecasts for 57 cents, on sales of $468.3 million, below forecasts for $469.2 million.
GrubHub (GRUB) has surged 19% to $83.50 after reporting a profit of 37 cents a share, beating forecasts for 31 cents, on sales of $205 million, beating estimates for $202 million. GrubHub also said it had 14.5 million diners during the quarter, well ahead of the 11.5 million predicted .
Hanesbrands (HBI) has tumbled 9.8% to $19.80 after meeting earnings forecasts but missing on sales and offering below-consensus guidance.
Illustration: Bloomberg News iRobot (IRBT) has tumbled after reporting a profit of 16 cents a share , missing forecasts for 25 cents, on sales of $326.9 million, topping forecasts for $318.8 million. iRobot said it would earn between $2.10 to $2.35 a share in 2018, well below forecasts for $2.70.
L Brands (LB) climbed 4.9% to $51.50 after reporting better-than-expected January same-store sales .
Philip Morris International (PM) has advanced 1.6% to $100.48 after missing earnings forecasts but beating on sales.
Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (REGN) has gained 4.1% to $348.48 after reporting better-than-expected fourth-quarter earnings and sales . "These beats were driven by strong Eylea sales across all geographies and above consensus gross and operating margins," writes Leerink analyst Geoffrey Porges.
Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) has after reporting a profit of 21 cents a share on sales of $653 million. Analysts had predicted earnings of 10 cents a share of sales of $664 million.
Teva Pharmaceutical Industries (TEVA) has tumbled 9.8% to $18.80 after beating fourth-quarter earnings and sales forecasts but offering 2018 earnings guidance that was a fraction of what had been expected . "With estimates for branded revenue recovery likely coming down, the argument for mid-term (2-4 years) recovery got tougher," writes Bernstein analyst Aaron Gal.
Tyson Foods (TSN) has climbed 4.9% to $77.00 after reporting better-than-expected first-quarter earnings and sales and offering consensus-topping full-year guidance .
Twitter (TWTR) has surged 20% to $32.33 after reporting its first profitable quarter .
Viacom (VIAB) has fallen 3.3% to $29.51 after reporting stronger than expected earnings but missing on sales . "Viacom once again came into the quarter with low investor expectations...and once again failed to achieve them," writes Bernstein analyst Todd Juenger.
XL Group (XL) has dropped 3.2% to $40.67 despite getting upgraded to Hold from Sell at Deutsche Bank following yesterday's takeover-inspired gain of 12%.
Yelp (YELP) has slumped 6.1% to $42.19 after reporting a profit of 19 cents a share on sales of $218.2 million. Analysts had been forecasting earnings of 27 cents a share on revenue of $215 million.
Yum China Holdings (YUMC) has dropped 4.7% to $42.24 after reporting adjusted earnings of 19 cents a share on sales of $2.2 billion. Analysts had predicted a profit 18 cents on revenue of $2.15 billion."Valuation multiples are ahead of local peers, and we see more limited EPS upside ahead as YUMC invests in quality, and as food and labor inflation offset top line," says Bernstein analyst Sara Senatore.
Hedge Funds: Good Month, Bad Month? January was the best month for hedge funds since December 2010 as they rode the equity markets' surge , according to new data from Hedge Fund Research.
Illustration: Getty Images “After a historic year in 2017, hedge funds began 2018 extending strong gains, even as realized and implied volatility associated with global equities, currencies (including cryptocurrencies), commodities, fixed income and the outlook for global inflation all increased,” HFR President Kenneth Heinz said in a statement.
The HFRI Fund Weighted Composite Index gained 2.8% last month, extending its winning streak to 15 straight months.
With the stock markets' climb, strategies focused around equities beat those tied to other asset classes. The HFRI Equity Hedge (Total) Index gained 3%, led by technology and emerging markets-focused funds which added 5.9% and 5.1% respectively.
The best performing strategy overall was macro, with the HFRI Macro (Total) Index increasing 3.7%, for its best month since February 2008. Within that category, quantitative, trend-following CTA strategies jumped 4.8%, its best month since October 2008.
It appears that those gains for CTAs may not hold: an index of performance maintained by Societe Generale showed that such funds have dropped more than 5% since February 1 . CTAs tend to be caught wrong-footed if market moves are too abrupt.
Fund strategies focused around cryptocurrency and blockchain didn't fare very well. The HFR Blockchain Index dropped 9.2%, after surging 2,798% last year. — Mary Childs
The View From Silicon Valley There seems to be no end in sight to the great A.I. debate
Despite a high-profile report that contends artificial intelligence will help create more jobs than it eliminates by 2020 , and an analyst's claim that robots will benefit society, tech’s biggest names are leery.
Illustration: iStockphoto “I feel like sometimes we in tech, even, abdicate control: ‘(A.I.) is going to happen tomorrow and our best case is that we’re going to be domesticated cats or whatever,’” Microsoft (MSFT) Chief Executive Officer Satya Nadella said at the Economic Club in New York on Wednesday. “But no, it’s a choice. I’m not making fun of that as a consequence. It could happen, but only if we abdicate.”
Nadella, whose comments echo similar concerns from Elon Musk, Apple (AAPL) co-founder Steve Wozniak and theoretical physicist Stephen Hawking, is convinced Microsoft, a leading A.I. vendor, and society as a whole “have to do some of our very best work at skilling .... students in school or people who are displaced midcareer."
Then there is the school of thought that A.I. is good for the economy, as market researcher Gartner concluded in a new report. Job gains in health care, the public sector and education will easily outpace losses in manufacturing, it says, leading to the creation of 2.3 million jobs by 2020 (vs. the elimination of 1.8 million jobs). By 2025, A.I. will help create a net gain of 2 million new jobs, according to the report.
“There are a lot of kinds of dystopian fears that there’ll be mass unemployment, that everything will be done by robots,” Binya Even, a portfolio manager at Nanuk Asset Management, said in Sydney on Wednesday. “But if we look at the medium term, say the next five to 10 years, I think robots can be a very positive influence to society.”
Then again…
“People think of A.I. as a monolithic thing that is coming to get us, but it is an incremental in how it learns,” says Rurik Bradbury, global head of conversational strategy at LivePerson (LPSN), which is hiring actors and screenwriters to humanize bots on customer-service calls. Its goal is to assign bots to answer commonly asked questions from customers of banks, telcos, retailers and other large organizations, and leave the more complicated stuff to human operators.
He anticipates a big shift to the model in the next year or so and, ultimately, could reduce the human workforce by up to 50%. — Jon Swartz
